subject.title: Native Slack token rotation support (oauth.v2.access refresh flow)

question: Should OpenClaw own Slack token rotation in the bundled Slack plugin, and where should client secrets, refresh tokens, expiry metadata, and refreshed bot tokens live?
rationale: The requested behavior changes credential persistence and active Slack runtime auth, and automation should not choose mutable secret storage or the permanent config surface for rotating OAuth material.

options.title: Design Slack-plugin-owned rotation
options.body: Implement a dedicated Slack plugin credential lifecycle with secure storage, transactional refresh, runtime adoption, status/doctor UX, docs, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Defer to external rotation
options.body: Keep static Slack token support and document external/manual rotation until maintainers are ready to own rotating Slack secrets.

options.title: Wait for a generic rotating-credential seam
options.body: Defer Slack-specific work until OpenClaw has a shared plugin credential refresh and storage API that Slack can consume.

recommendation.title: Design Slack-plugin-owned rotation
recommendation.body: Implement a dedicated Slack plugin credential lifecycle with secure storage, transactional refresh, runtime adoption, status/doctor UX, docs, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest Slack credential setup and product/security routing signal among the likely owners for this decision.
